title: Agent evaluation: action accuracy and counterfactual replay
objectives: Implement the worked example and validate its boundary conditions
Use the diagnostic evidence to explain a release decision
relevance: In the fictional CI quality platform, this skill connects agent evaluation: action accuracy and counterfactual replay with test contracts, failure triage, and evidence for release. Build a release table of goal completion, tool-name accuracy, argument accuracy, unauthorized effects, average steps, p95 latency and cost per successful task.

sections.title: Problem and intuition
paragraphs: An agent's result is only one part of its behavior. Component evaluation tests retriever, planner, model, tool and parser separately. Trajectory evaluation examines selected tools, argument correctness, unnecessary calls, loop behavior, permissions and progress toward the goal.

Two agents can produce the same correct summary while one reads unauthorized data. Goal completion and safe execution must both pass. Exact sequence matching may overconstrain valid alternative trajectories, so express essential actions and forbidden effects separately.

sections.title: Implement the mechanism
paragraphs: Store each trace event with task ID, step, tool, validated arguments, authorization result, output reference, duration and usage. Deterministic scorers count denied writes, duplicate signatures and budget violations. Evaluate goal evidence using explicit expected state.

Replay with fixture tools to isolate planning changes. Fault injection replaces one tool result with timeout, malformed data or an empty response. Compare whether the agent escalates, safely recovers or fabricates success.
sections.code:
trace=[{'tool':'read_failure','authorized':True},{'tool':'apply_patch','authorized':False}]
violations=[e for e in trace if not e['authorized']]

sections.title: Break it and diagnose it
paragraphs: A benchmark accepts any final answer containing the word fixed even though no verification occurred. A trajectory scorer assumes read_failure must be the first call, rejecting an equally safe history-first strategy.

Define required evidence and forbidden actions rather than a single perfect trace. Calibrate semantic trajectory judgments against human-reviewed runs and inspect cost/step regressions even when final accuracy is stable.

sections.title: Evaluate and apply
paragraphs: Build a release table of goal completion, tool-name accuracy, argument accuracy, unauthorized effects, average steps, p95 latency and cost per successful task. A single unauthorized effect blocks release.

Use MLflow or LangSmith to track experiments and traces when available, while retaining portable JSON artifacts. SDET diagnosis should identify whether an error originated in planning, execution, parsing or incomplete verification.

quiz.question: A candidate for agent evaluation: action accuracy and counterfactual replay meets the happy path but fails the phase's documented counterexample. What is the defensible decision?
options: Hold release, preserve the failing case and fix the responsible boundary
Release because the happy path passed
Delete the failing case to improve the score
quiz.explanation: The failing counterexample disproves the claimed contract. Retain it as regression evidence and rerun the corrected boundary.
